_comment: The only per-repo file in this skill. SKILL.md and repos.md are identical
across every repo that uses /ai-dev — when you copy the skill to another
project, edit this file and nothing else.
'toolkit' is null here because this repo IS the toolkit. There is no companion
PR and no -Plunula.toolkit.path: a Lunula ticket's own PR is the toolkit change.
basePort is deliberately distinct from Lunicle's (8090) and Lunamux's (8460).
All three automations can be sweeping at the same time on one machine, and a
shared port would have them fight over it across repos.
runInstructions: This repo ships an in-tree demo app under demo/ that exercises the toolkit as a
pure consumer. It is the right way to verify almost any toolkit change, and it
costs nothing to run: no server, no database, no sign-in.
./gradlew :demo:web:jsBrowserDevelopmentExecutableDistribution
python3 -m http.server {port} --bind 127.0.0.1 \
--directory demo/web/build/dist/js/developmentExecutable
http.server blocks until killed — background it (run_in_background, or `… &`) and
poll the URL until it answers. In the foreground it hangs you until you time out,
with nothing verified.
Then browse http://127.0.0.1:{port}/. The bundle is served off disk, so after an
edit just re-run the distribution task and reload — no restart.
Do not use ./gradlew :demo:web:jsBrowserDevelopmentRun. Its webpack dev server
takes its port from the build script rather than the command line, so every
concurrent ticket would try to bind the same one. Serving the built distribution
on your assigned {port} is what keeps parallel sweeps from colliding. The build
directory is per-worktree, so nothing else needs isolating.
Kill the server you started when you are done.
A change the demo cannot reach — a Compose-only surface, or something only a real
consumer exercises — is a Verification gap. Say so in the PR. Do NOT go and build
Lunicle or Lunamux against your branch to prove it: that is a much larger job than
the ticket, and those checkouts belong to other tickets that may be running now.
